description: `review-policy --lane TASK_ID` still classifies a lane whose branch is already gone -- `--prune` reclaims a cleanly merged lane's branch (`git branch -d`) once it lands, which would otherwise leave `worktrees.lane_diff`/`mv_engine::lane_diff::lane_diff` with nothing to diff against. This scenario's lane (see `projects.sandbox.lanes` -- conformance/README.md 'Lane fixtures', `"merge": true`) is `--no-ff` merged into the project's main branch (commit subject `Merge branch 'multiverse/<task_id>'`, git's own default message) and then its branch is deleted, simulating exactly that reclaim. `_merged_lane_tip`/`merged_lane_tip` must recover the lane's last commit from the merge commit's second parent rather than refusing with 'no branch to diff against', so the touched-file classification (the same `auth` risk-path override as review-policy-lane-risk-path.json) still resolves. Read-only: no Herdr call.
